name: Jacob
title: The Patriarch Who Wrestled with God
summary: Jacob, also called Israel, was the son of Isaac and Rebekah, and the grandson of Abraham. He had twelve sons who became the ancestors of the twelve tribes of Israel. His life was marked by struggle, cunning, divine encounters, and ultimately reconciliation, and he plays a central role in God's covenant history.

keyEvents.title: Jacob's Birth and the Right of the Firstborn
keyEvents.description: Jacob was born as a twin with Esau, holding onto Esau's heel. Later, he bought the birthright from Esau for a meal of lentil stew.

keyEvents.title: Jacob Deceives His Father to Receive the Blessing
keyEvents.description: With the help of his mother Rebekah, Jacob tricked his father Isaac into giving him the blessing meant for Esau by dressing in goat skins.

keyEvents.title: Jacob's Dream at Bethel
keyEvents.description: Fleeing from Esau, Jacob dreamed of a ladder reaching up to heaven with angels going up and down, and God confirmed the covenant promises to him.

keyEvents.title: Jacob Wrestles with God at Peniel
keyEvents.description: Jacob wrestled with a heavenly figure through the night and received the new name Israel, which means 'he who struggles with God'.

keyEvents.title: Reconciliation with Esau
keyEvents.description: After many years, Jacob met his brother Esau again, and the two were reconciled in a moving encounter marked by grace and forgiveness.

keyEvents.title: Jacob Goes to Egypt and Blesses His Sons
keyEvents.description: In his old age, Jacob went to Egypt to be reunited with his son Joseph. Before his death, he blessed his twelve sons with prophetic words about their future.
